chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:

I asked him, 'When does the ritual bath (ghusl) become obligatory upon the man and the woman?' He said, 'When he enters her, then the ritual bath, the dower (mahr), and the stoning (rajm) become obligatory.'
ai.seo_question: When does ghusl become obligatory for men and women according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes that sexual penetration (dakhala) is the specific trigger for the obligation of major ritual bath (ghusl al-janabah) for both men and women. It further links this physical act to the legal consequences of full dower (mahr) and, for a free woman, the penalty of stoning (rajm) in cases of adultery, highlighting the jurisprudential connection between physical intimacy and marital rights. This narration is foundational in Shia fiqh for defining the boundaries of janabah and its associated legal rulings.
